ai.description: This slender snake reaches 40–50 cm. It is brown above with a distinct black-spotted yellow collar and a dark head. The venter is pale with a row of black dots along each side of the belly.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *Sibynophis subpunctatus* by the distinct dark, transverse bar or "collar" on the nape, which is bordered posteriorly by a prominent pale yellow or white band.
ai.habitat: Sibynophis subpunctatus inhabits moist deciduous forests and scrublands, typically found in hilly regions and lower mountain slopes up to an altitude of 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Sibynophis subpunctatus is primarily a diurnal, ground-dwelling snake that actively hunts for small lizards and skinks among leaf litter and rocky crevices.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sibynophis subpunctatus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Sibynophis subpunctatus occurs across the Indian subcontinent, primarily in the Western Ghats, central India, and the Himalayan foothills, ranging from sea level to 2,000m.
